scope: Three texture directions applied offline to unchanged approved masks. No Godot integration.

variants.name: A · Crypte humide
variants.direction: ANCIENT DAMP CRYPT, evil through decay and contamination. Deep blue-slate, rough broken mineral facets, irregular eroded shallow pits, ingrained soot, patchy black damp staining and sparse desaturated sickly violet mineral deposits. Aged long-abandoned stone with lower-value soaked areas and a few delicate damp edge glints, mostly matte. Wall visibly rough and pitted, with a few worn chipped scars. Floor similarly worn with dark damp patches, a few hairline cracks and sparse grit. Wood old water-blackened oak with coarse but sparse worn grain and small split scars, cold grey-brown. Iron mottled black oxidation and pitting, very sparse cold dull worn glints. A FEW tiny faint violet spores/stains only, not strong neon veins, not green moss blanket. No large roots. Rich readable painted surface, no concrete slab look.
variants.prompt:
Create ONE square 2x2 MATERIAL TEXTURE ATLAS for a hand-painted stylized evil/corrupted 2D dungeon game. The first reference is the user's original game mockup: imitate its gloomy slate-blue masonry, chunky painterly shapes, localized violet corruption and strong readability, but create MATERIALS ONLY. The second reference is the current material board, rejected as too clean and smooth: you must add conspicuous age, roughness and evil character while keeping a coherent family. Output exactly FOUR equal square quadrants, with a thin straight central horizontal and vertical separator at exactly 50%. TOP LEFT is a continuous exposed wall stone surface; TOP RIGHT is a calmer walked-on FLOOR stone surface from the same mineral family; BOTTOM LEFT is continuous weathered wooden DOOR surface with vertical grain; BOTTOM RIGHT is continuous forged IRON hardware surface. All four swatches are full-bleed flat OPAQUE material surfaces, no architecture, no bricks or slab divisions, no mortar, no door shape, no plank boundaries, no border frame, no lettering, no objects. Each quadrant is one continuous material, later clipped to exact approved geometry. Matte, dark but clearly legible, substantial hand-painted facets and chips; no photographic noise, no tiny scratch carpet, no smooth plastic, no featureless black. Wood desaturated grey-brown/charcoal, no orange. Iron cold dark blue-grey. Floor 65-75% calm readable stone with the more striking damage confined to pockets; stone remains visible. No torches, no characters, no UI. Three related styles are being compared; this image represents only the following single direction:
ANCIENT DAMP CRYPT, evil through decay and contamination. Deep blue-slate, rough broken mineral facets, irregular eroded shallow pits, ingrained soot, patchy black damp staining and sparse desaturated sickly violet mineral deposits. Iron mottled black oxidation and pitting, very sparse cold dull worn glints. A FEW tiny faint violet spores/stains only, not strong neon veins, not green moss blanket. No large roots. Rich readable painted surface, no concrete slab look.

variants.name: B · Pierre maudite
variants.direction: ARCANE CURSED STONE, malignant energy buried inside fractured masonry. Deep indigo-slate broken mineral faces, sharp chips, recessed black fissures and a SMALL NUMBER of branching violet-magenta emissive seams. Stone damage and age clearly visible; high quality layered painterly facets. Luminous detail covers only about 4% of surface, clustered asymmetrically with 65% quieter breathing space. In each stone sample only two or three localized fine branching purple fissure groups, with tight restrained bloom and very dark charred borders; NO lava rivers, no all-over electric network, no giant crystals. Floor has fewer thinner purple seams and visibly worn matte patches; leave the main surface calm. Door is charcoal-brown aged timber, dry worn grain, a few dark fissures infiltrated by dim violet traces. Iron black-blue, pitted and tarnished with one sparse purple pit cluster and subdued edge wear. These are flat material maps, no casts or protruding shapes.

variants.name: C · Corruption organique
variants.direction: ORGANIC CORRUPTION, the masonry is slowly infected by black root-like growth. Rough dark blue slate with worn chipped facets and damp dirty pockets. Sparse coal-black, angular, sinewy root veins visibly embedded in shallow fractures, carrying very faint purple capillaries. Dark tendrils should occupy about 15% of the wall material, concentrated in one or two asymmetrical areas with 65% calm visible stone. Root strands are small relative to swatch, flattened into surface, NOT oversized branches, NO roots crossing the atlas separators, NO giant tentacles, NO bones or skulls. Floor carries a much thinner sparser root scar near one corner and weathered pitted stone; passage remains visually quiet. Wood grey-brown blackened rotting old oak, a few split grain channels colonized by dark root filaments and a pinprick of violet. Iron is soot-black and pitted, with sparse embedded dark fibrous scars and a little cool blue-grey wear. Sinister and tactile but still stylized painterly and readable, no slime blanket.
